summary: Months after the 1906 fire the Board allowed refugee cottages to go up on Pennsylvania Avenue. For twenty-five years after that it was mostly blasting and grading this hill into streets, and granting soap works and railroads the spur tracks to reach them. In 1918 Mrs M. Hornick was allowed to keep one cow at 831 Kansas Street; the following year Dorothy Kostrikin was refused a stable on Twenty-third. In 1930 St Teresa's School was given permission to rope off Pennsylvania Street twice each morning so the children could go outside.

summary_sources.t: Permitting Erection of Cottages for Refugees on Pennsylvania Avenue.
